config.title: Build billing usage aggregation pipeline

intro.title: Build billing usage aggregation pipeline
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a billing usage aggregation pipeline that processes raw usage data from multiple sources into a single, summarized report. You will learn how to use Node.js to read data from files, transform it by grouping and summing values, and write the aggregated results to a new file. The core programming concept is data aggregation using arrays and objects to collect and compute totals. You'll work with Node.js's built-in 'fs' module for file operations and JavaScript methods like 'map' and 'reduce' for data manipulation. This project will help you understand how to handle real-world data processing tasks in a backend environment.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building backend billing and analytics systems in SaaS platforms like Stripe, AWS, or Shopify. Developers implement usage aggregation pipelines to process raw event data—such as API calls, storage usage, or compute time—into summarized, billable metrics for customer dashboards and invoices. For example, a cloud service dashboard might display aggregated monthly usage statistics and cost breakdowns, which are generated by similar pipelines that transform logs into actionable insights. Mastering this skill enables you to create scalable, accurate billing systems that handle high volumes of transactional data efficiently.

objectives: Construct a Node.js script to read and parse raw usage data from a JSON file
Implement a function to aggregate usage data by customer ID and service type
Configure a data transformation pipeline to calculate total usage and cost per customer
Initialize and manipulate a data structure to store aggregated billing results
Integrate file system operations to write the aggregated results to a new JSON file
Apply error handling to manage missing data or file read/write failures
Control the execution flow of the pipeline to process data sequentially

steps.instruction: Import the fs (file system) and path modules using require() statements.
steps.hint: Use require('fs') and require('path') to import the modules.

successCriteria: fs and path modules are imported using require() statements.

steps.title: Initialize the usage aggregation object
steps.instruction: Inside your async function, create an empty object named aggregatedUsage to store customer billing totals.

// Example: creating an empty object
const emptyObject = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: An empty aggregatedUsage object is created inside your function.
successCriteria: The aggregatedUsage object is declared inside the function body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the aggregatedUsage object. This will serve as the container for storing aggregated billing data per customer.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created an empty object named aggregatedUsage inside your function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The aggregatedUsage object wasn't found inside your function. Remember to create an empty object using curly braces {}.

steps.title: Read the input directory contents
steps.instruction: Inside the aggregateBillingUsage function, use await fs.readdir() to get an array of file names from the input directory parameter. Store the result in a variable named 'files'.
steps.hint: Use the fs module's readdir method with the input directory path. Remember to use await since readdir returns a promise.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: reading files from a directory
const files = await fs.readdir('./input-folder');
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will be able to read all file names from the specified input directory and store them in a 'files' variable for processing.
successCriteria: The aggregateBillingUsage function contains a line that uses await fs.readdir() with the input directory parameter and stores the result in a 'files' variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the directory reading logic. The 'files' variable now contains all the file names from the input directory.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using await with fs.readdir() and storing the result in a variable named 'files'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The directory reading logic isn't quite right. You need to use await fs.readdir() with the input directory path and store the result in a variable.

steps.title: Create helper function to parse billing files
steps.instruction: Inside your aggregateBillingUsage function, define an async helper function named parseBillingFile that takes a filePath parameter.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember it should be async and accept one parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an async parseBillingFile function defined inside aggregateBillingUsage, ready to implement file parsing logic in later steps.
successCriteria: The parseBillingFile function is defined as async, takes a filePath parameter, and is placed inside the aggregateBillingUsage function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the parseBillingFile helper function. This will be essential for processing individual billing files in our aggregation pipeline.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure parseBillingFile is defined as an async function inside aggregateBillingUsage and accepts a filePath parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parseBillingFile helper function needs to be defined. Create an async function named parseBillingFile that takes a filePath parameter inside your aggregateBillingUsage function.

steps.title: Implement file reading in the helper
steps.instruction: Inside the parseBillingFile helper function, use fs.readFile to read the file content and parse it as JSON.
steps.hint: Use await fs.readFile with 'utf-8' encoding, then parse the result with JSON.parse.
steps.expectedOutcome: The parseBillingFile function will be able to read JSON billing files and return parsed data.
successCriteria: parseBillingFile uses await fs.readFile with 'utf-8' encoding and JSON.parse to return parsed JSON data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented file reading and JSON parsing in the helper function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using await with fs.readFile and parsing the result with JSON.parse.
steps.feedbackWrong: The helper function doesn't yet read files or parse JSON. Try using fs.readFile with 'utf-8' encoding and JSON.parse.

steps.title: Process each billing file in the directory
steps.instruction: Inside the aggregateBillingUsage function, after reading the directory contents, add a for...of loop to iterate through the file names and call parseBillingFile for each file.
steps.hint: Use a for...of loop to process each file name from the directory listing. For each file, construct the full file path and call the parseBillingFile helper function with await.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will iterate through all billing files in the directory and process each one using the parseBillingFile helper.
successCriteria: A for...of loop is implemented that iterates through file names, constructs full file paths, and calls parseBillingFile with await for each file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the file iteration logic. The loop will process each billing file one by one.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using a for...of loop to iterate through the file names and calling parseBillingFile for each one.
steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation doesn't match the expected structure. You need to add a for...of loop to process each billing file in the directory.

steps.title: Aggregate usage data from parsed files
steps.instruction: Inside the for...of loop, after calling parseBillingFile, add each file's usage amount to the aggregatedUsage object for the corresponding customer.
steps.hint: For each parsed file, access the customer and amount properties, then add the amount to the existing total for that customer in aggregatedUsage.
steps.expectedOutcome: The aggregatedUsage object will accumulate total usage amounts per customer as each file is processed.
successCriteria: The for...of loop includes code that adds each file's usage amount to the aggregatedUsage object under the correct customer key.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the aggregation logic. The usage amounts are now being summed per customer.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the aggregation logic might be incomplete. Make sure you're adding the amount to the existing total for each customer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The aggregation step is missing or incorrect. Inside the loop, you need to update aggregatedUsage with the parsed file data.

steps.title: Create helper function to write aggregated data
steps.instruction: Inside the aggregateBillingUsage function, define an async helper function named writeAggregatedData that takes two parameters: aggregatedData and outputFilePath.
steps.hint: Add the function definition after your existing parseBillingFile helper function, before the for...of loop. Use the async keyword and function declaration syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new async helper function defined that can later be used to write the aggregated billing data to a file.
successCriteria: The writeAggregatedData function is defined with async keyword, takes two parameters (aggregatedData and outputFilePath), and is placed inside aggregateBillingUsage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the writeAggregatedData helper function. This function will be used in the next step to save the aggregated billing data to a file.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined an async function named writeAggregatedData that takes two parameters: aggregatedData and outputFilePath. Check that it's placed inside the aggregateBillingUsage function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition doesn't match the requirements. You need to define an async function named writeAggregatedData inside aggregateBillingUsage that accepts aggregatedData and outputFilePath as parameters.

steps.title: Implement file writing in the helper
steps.instruction: Inside the writeAggregatedData helper function, implement the file writing logic using fs.writeFile to save the aggregated data as formatted JSON to the output file.
steps.hint: Use fs.writeFile with the output file path, JSON.stringify to convert the data to a formatted JSON string, and handle any errors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The writeAggregatedData helper function will be able to write the aggregated billing data to a JSON file with proper formatting.
successCriteria: The writeAggregatedData function uses fs.writeFile to write JSON.stringify(aggregatedData, null, 2) to the specified output path and includes error handling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the file writing helper function. It will save the aggregated billing data as formatted JSON.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use JSON.stringify with proper formatting (null, 2) and include error handling in your implementation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file writing logic isn't quite right. Remember to use fs.writeFile with the output path and convert the aggregated data to a formatted JSON string using JSON.stringify.

steps.title: Call the write function in main
steps.instruction: Inside the aggregateBillingUsage function, after the for...of loop, call the writeAggregatedData helper function with the aggregatedUsage object and an output file path.
steps.hint: Use await with the function call since writeAggregatedData is async. Pass aggregatedUsage as the second argument and a string like './output/aggregated.json' as the first argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main function will now write the aggregated usage data to an output file after processing all billing files.
successCriteria: writeAggregatedData is called with aggregatedUsage and an output file path after the for...of loop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the aggregation logic with the output writing logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling writeAggregatedData with both arguments: an output file path and the aggregatedUsage object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the function call. You need to call writeAggregatedData with the aggregated data and output path after processing all files.

steps.title: Add error handling and export the function
steps.instruction: Wrap the main logic inside your aggregateBillingUsage function with a try-catch block and export the function using module.exports.
steps.hint: Place the try block around the existing code inside the function body. In the catch block, log the error. Then add module.exports = aggregateBillingUsage; at the bottom of the file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The aggregateBillingUsage function will have error handling and be exported for use in other modules.
successCriteria: The main logic is wrapped in a try-catch block, errors are logged in the catch block, and the function is exported using module.exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error handling and exported the function, making it ready for use in other parts of your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've wrapped all the main logic in the try block and added the module.exports statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've wrapped the existing code in a try-catch block and added the export statement at the bottom of the file.
